title: Claude placed my HUD fine. It never decided when to show it
author: flockbaygames
selftext:
I asked Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code for a top-down twin-stick shooter in Godot 4 with a health bar, an ammo count and a score. All three came back in the corners away from the middle, and at 1280x800 like a Steam Deck the whole picture kept its 16:9 shape with bars above and below and the HUD came along.

So placement wasn't the problem. In a fresh run I gave it the same sentence plus a HUD description: health bottom left, ammo bottom right beside the weapon's name, score small at the top, a 5% safe margin on every side, and health and ammo fading out after three seconds with no change and coming straight back when they change or health is low.

That one filled the Steam Deck screen with no bars, the HUD sat inside its margin, and the health bar faded when I stopped taking hits and was straight back on the next one. It also wrote a test that fails if anything enters the middle of the screen, though with only file tools it couldn't run it.

My takeaway is to describe a HUD by its moments and not only its corners: what fades, what comes back, what stays out of the middle. Fading is a taste call though, in a game where you count every bullet it's one more thing to wait for.

What's the cleanest HUD you've played with?
